cards.explanation: The answer is the islands and distant peoples. The Servant says, "Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples…" (Isaiah 49:1). He isn't whispering to the folks next door, friends. He's calling to people way out past the horizon, and I love a speaker who thinks that big.

The answer is quiver. The Servant says, "He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver." (Isaiah 49:2). A quiver is the case that holds arrows, so this arrow is tucked away close. Polished AND tucked in, friends. That's a well-kept arrow.

The answer is True. The LORD says to the Servant, "You are My Servant, Israel, in whom I will display My glory." (Isaiah 49:3). The LORD says He will display His glory in this Servant. That's a mighty big thing to be told, bakers.

The answer is God. Even in the middle of that hard moment, the Servant says, "yet My vindication is with the LORD, and My reward is with My God." (Isaiah 49:4). Notice the "yet," friends. He's worn out, but he doesn't stop there. He says where the reward is.

The answer is that He is honored in the LORD's sight. The Servant says, "…for I am honored in the sight of the LORD, and My God is My strength…" (Isaiah 49:5). Just before this, He said He had spent His strength (Isaiah 49:4). Honored in the LORD's sight AND God is His strength. That's a good place to stand, bakers.

The answer is a light for the nations. The LORD says, "I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth." (Isaiah 49:6). The job grows past Jacob's tribes and reaches the ends of the earth, friends. That's one big light.

The answer is bow down. The LORD says, "Kings will see You and rise, and princes will bow down…" (Isaiah 49:7). Remember who He's talking to: the One who was despised and abhorred by the nation. Kings standing up and princes bowing is a big turn, bakers.

The answer is False. The verse says kings and princes honor Him "…because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen You." (Isaiah 49:7). No army is mentioned, friends. It all comes from the LORD who chose Him, and that's a good reason to bow.

The answer is help. The LORD says, "In the time of favor I will answer You, and in the day of salvation I will help You…" (Isaiah 49:8). Answer and help, back to back, friends. I'd call that a promise worth writing on the oven door.

The answer is "Come out." The Servant is appointed "to say to the prisoners, 'Come out'" (Isaiah 49:9). Two little words for the prisoners, bakers. I know a thing or two about waiting in a dark drawer, so I like those words a LOT.

The answer is False. The text says, "They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun beat down on them." (Isaiah 49:10). That follows verse 9, where they feed along the pathways and find pasture on barren hills. They're taken care of the whole way, friends.

The answer is beside springs of water. "For He who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them beside springs of water." (Isaiah 49:10). The guide is the One who has compassion on them, bakers. A walk beside springs of water sounds like a pretty good way to travel.

The answer is people from far away. The LORD says, "Behold, they will come from far away, from the north and from the west, and from the land of Aswan." (Isaiah 49:12). People are on the way, friends, coming from the north, the west and Aswan. A full house is on its way.

The answer is True. The text says, "Shout for joy, O heavens; rejoice, O earth; break forth in song, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people…" (Isaiah 49:13). The reason is right there after the "For," bakers. The LORD has comforted His people, and the heavens, the earth and the mountains each get a call to celebrate.

The answer is compassion. The passage closes with "…He will have compassion on His afflicted ones." (Isaiah 49:13). Compassion also showed up in verse 10, where the One who has compassion on them leads them beside springs of water. That's a gentle place to land, friends.
